messages:
mira: Heads-up — proposing a temporary pin of the runtime to v2.14.7 for the model rollout next week. Suggest change window Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC. Root cause: a kernel selection path in v3.0-rc1 leads to sporadic kv-cache validation errors on quantized longseq runs.

sam: Can you paste the failing log excerpt so infra can triage? We saw something similar during the llama3q trial.

mira: Sure — minimal repro: ```
ERROR kv_cache: validation failed: expected 0x1a but got 0x00 at seq 128
  at /srv/runtime/kv_cache.c:412
  model=llama3q-quant v0.9
Repro: longseq > 8k tokens, continuous batching on g4dn-type hw.
```

olivia: If we pin runtime to 2.14.7, what's the SDK surface fallout? The SDK shim 1.9.x expects runtime >=3.0 for some new APIs. Any mandatory breakage?

lee: SDK shim 1.9.* uses the new runtime API for streaming handles, but falls back for basic generation. Main concern is routing & dedicated customers who are pinned to newer runtime—they could see degraded features. We'll need a short compatibility note.

jonah: Ran a quick compat matrix: runtime v3.0-rc1 + SDK 1.9.2 -> shortseq PASS, longseq FAIL on quant models. Recommended plan: pin hosted to v2.14.7 for the initial rollout window, enable a 1% canary first; provide dedicated customers opt-in to rc1 if they accept potential errors.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: pin runtime -> v2.14.7 for hosted-prod at 2026-03-03T02:00:00Z. Author: mira. Change window: 2h. Estimated completion: 15m.

carla: Quick question — why v2.14.7 specifically vs a patched rc1? Is there a patch ready?

mira: 2.14.7 is the last stable we validated against quant models under longseq. The kernel patch that fixes the mismatch is still in review in runtime repo. We don't want to block the model rollout, hence the temporary pin. Patch target for rc1->stable is next week.

olivia: SRE note: we'll create alerts for kv_cache error-rate > 0.5% and a p95 latency spike > 250ms. Can we do a canary at 1% traffic for 30m, then 10% if healthy? If issues surface, we roll back to pre-pin routing.

sam: Agreed. Also need an SDK snippet for customers: recommend calling the shim explicitly while pinned: ```python
client.set_runtime_version('2.14.7')
```

jonah: Rollout script suggestion: ```bash
deployctl pin runtime --version 2.14.7 --scope hosted --canary 0.01 --step 10m
```

deploy-bot: Action: canary started (1% traffic). Canary ID: cb-2045. Hosts: hosted-us-west-prod-1..3. Author: mira.

lee: I'm watching dashboards for kv_cache errors and memory regressions. Will call if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

carla: If we need to rollback, what's the exact rollback path and who clicks it?

mira: Rollback path: `deployctl unpin --scope hosted --reason "canary-fail"` which reverts routing to last compatible candidate. I'll own the rollback. Escalation: if errors >15m at canary -> immediate rollback; if after widen, rollback and open incident. I'll also prepare customer-facing release notes and a brief postmortem template.

olivia: Also update support playbook: steps to opt-out/opt-in for dedicated customers and a canned customer message.

sam: I'll draft a short release-note in #eng-releases after canary stabilizes.

deploy-bot: Canary cb-2045 status: healthy for 18m. No kv_cache spikes detected. Next step: widen to 10% at 10:15 UTC.

mira: Thanks — if widen is green we'll proceed with full pin and then follow-up with a scheduled dev runtime patch. I'll publish the compatibility badge and SDK guidance once complete.
